Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. That matches our notes. A few clarifications from our security/compliance team:

- SOC 2: we need the latest SOC 2 Type II report (or a summary if the full report is not shared due to vendor policy) plus the scope (which services and data centers were in scope).
- Data regs: while our immediate scope is financial data (no PHI), we still need confirmation on GDPR data processing if EU customers appear, and confirmation that Redwood supports contractual BAA if a future use includes PHI.
- Pen test: please confirm whether you perform annual third-party pen tests and whether you can share the latest pen-test report (redacted if necessary). If not available, please provide your vulnerability management policy including scan cadence, severity-based SLA for remediation, and your coordinated disclosure process.

I've attached our vendor security questionnaire for you to start (Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-FinHealth.docx). We typically expect the vendor questionnaire back within 7 business days for initial vendor review. Also please let us know if there are any NDAs/DPAs we need to sign before we can accept certain artifacts.

Thanks — Jamie

Jamie — great, thanks for the questionnaire. We're happy to comply with your timeline. Quick responses below and attached artifacts: Redwood-SOC2-Summary-2026.pdf and Redwood-Pentest-Info-2026.pdf.

SOC 2:
- We completed a SOC 2 Type II in May 2026. We can share a summary (attached) publicly; for the full report we typically require an MSA/nda and a confidential distribution agreement — happy to sign what you need. The summary includes in-scope systems and locations.

GDPR/BAA:
- GDPR: we have data processing addenda and standard contractual clauses available for EU processing — we will loop in legal if you want the DPA.
- BAA: Redwood supports customer-specific BAAs for customers who require PHI controls; please flag if you're likely to expand into PHI so we can accelerate that discussion.

Pen test & Vulnerability Management (short answer, full doc attached):
- Third-party pen tests: annual, last completed March 2026 by an external assessor; we can share a redacted report after an NDA/Confidentiality confirmation.
- Scanning cadence: weekly authenticated internal scans, nightly unauthenticated perimeter scans, and on-commit static analysis for our infra-as-code.
- Remediation SLA: Critical/high: 7 days for mitigation plan/patch schedule; Medium: 30 days; Low: 90 days (exceptions documented).
- Disclosure process: coordinated disclosure; we accept reports via a dedicated security inbox and coordinate with the reporter and impacted customers; we publish CVE/mitigation notes for high-severity infra issues when disclosure is appropriate.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) We're attaching the two docs now.
2) We'll start the vendor questionnaire and aim to return answers within 5 business days.
3) Rishi can do a 30-minute technical call to walk your security team through scope and any live questions — propose Wed 7/28 or Thu 7/29.

Let us know which date/time works and if you want the NDA first.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-Summary-2026.pdf, Redwood-Pentest-Info-2026.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Jamie — quick technical clarifications from the engineering/security side (copied from the pen-test doc for convenience):

- Scope: Standard customer-facing production endpoints (API + console). Internal SRE and customer data stores are in scope only when explicitly agreed; by default we limit scope to the customer-facing surfaces.
- Pen test type: our last test was a credentialed assessment (authenticated with test credentials for representative user roles) plus external black-box reconnaissance. If FinHealth has specific tests (e.g., social engineering / phishing), we need explicit authorization and scoping.
- Test artifacts: we can share the pen test report with redactions for customer data and certain exploit PoCs; full technical appendices can be shared under NDA.
- Vulnerability disclosure & SLA: for Critical (CVSS >=9.0) we triage within 24 hours and target mitigations or controls within 7 days; for High (7.0-8.9) we aim for mitigation plan within 72 hours and remediation within 30 days. We retain a public disclosure cadence for issues that affect multiple customers.
- Issue tracking: we provide ticket IDs and status updates via a customer security portal (or via email if you prefer).

If you want we can include sample redacted pages from the March 2026 report in the NDA package so you can validate depth of coverage.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
